batch_observations:
ELEVEN PLAYS, AND THE BATCH SPLITS ALMOST EXACTLY IN HALF ON A SINGLE PROPERTY: whether the play was ever allowed to lose. Five (chain_polarity_flip, covering_self_limiting_cot_wow_gate, price_free_absorption_proxy, eia_window_reopen_to_print, burn_is_demand_arrival_not_direction) carry at least one measurement that came out badly and was published anyway - a refuted ratio arm, a refuted mirror arm, a withdrawn fire, a 5x mass refutation, a predecessor retired on its own named forward test. Five (storage_thursday_magnitude, squeeze_ignition_flush_conjunction, shoulder_counter_print_damping, giveback_exhaustion_reversal_recognition, eia_preprint_overextension_gate) are built out of days that already happened, and every counterexample produced a NEW conditioning dimension rather than a refutation. One (book_contrarian) rests on a single pooled number nobody can re-test because the instrument is served nowhere.

THE ONE HARD CONTRADICTION IN THE RECORD. daytype.eia_preprint_overextension_gate's declined_evidence says of G20: 'Run honestly on both days, only tell (b) fires on each - below the 2-of-3 bar - so the gate EXPLICITLY SPARED the full band on both.' The committed BLIND posterior says the opposite in its own day_class field: 'PRE-PRINT OVER-EXTENSION GATE FIRED -> two-sided / counter-tilt, chain-sided full band REFUSED' (research/kalshi/forecasts/g20_blind_round1/grp20_mbo_specialist_D.json, 20260528). Both statements are about the same day. The reconciliation is mechanical and it is worse than a bookkeeping error: limb (a) is denominated in DOLLARS of chain cum, which is price content and masked, so in the BLIND it was scored 'HALF - fired on the flow proxy' and pushed the gate over its 2-of-3 bar, while in the price-bearing REFINE the same limb came back a clean NO ('same-side run 1 day at +610 vs the ~900 bar'). The brain merged the refine's account of a gate that only ever has to work in the blind. The day was +2,100 actual against a +150 emission - the walk's largest single-day miss.

THE S108 SIGNATURE IS PRESENT AND I NAMED IT WHERE I FOUND IT, but the more common defect in this batch is a different one: A CONDITION THAT CANNOT CHANGE STATE. Measured on the served corpus: magnitude.shoulder_counter_print_damping's ~20 gw-HDD bar fires 40 of 40 days in g20-g23 on every HDD instrument served (realized 0.0-1.5, fwd7 span max 4.348) - the actual discriminator in the field is the untestable word 'SHOULDER', and D's 0702 stand-down declines on prose ('S2 summer with the demand mass actually delivering') rather than on the number. squeeze_watch.active is 10-of-10 or 0-of-10 in all six blocks, never a within-block transition, 10 active days of 60. structure.chain_polarity_flip's C1 is UNKNOWABLE in the blind (it needs the prior day's net) - five G22/G23 posteriors say so in their own words - which directly contradicts the play's own requires field. eia_preprint limb (b) arm 1 compares session_b_share to 0.50 on a series that clears 0.50 on 2 of 47 non-Monday days, so one side is a near-constant and on the two-sided series the limb's verdict FLIPS on 3 of the 6 Thursdays where both are served.

WHAT SURPRISED ME MOST. positioning.covering_self_limiting_cot_wow_gate is BETTER than its thin n=2 evidence suggests - its falsifiability clause is a real constraint that fires, and I verified two correct refusals in a committed refine posterior where the gate changed the number by zero. But its input has a defect nobody has recorded: on the two seams where the COT report is re-served STALE at age 9.35 days, the IDENTICAL reading preceded OPPOSITE-signed gaps both times (MM -122,617 / WoW -7,763 -> 0615 gap -750 and 0622 gap +1,210; MM -82,722 / WoW +2,187 -> 0629 gap +50 and 0706 gap -580). Two natural experiments, both negative, both invisible in the brain.

D23 NOTE FOR GREG, since it is what the numbers keep pointing at: the healthiest condition in this batch is COT MM WoW, which is a DELTA sited at the centre of its own distribution (range -38,123 to +23,762 over 12 seams, 10 distinct values, and it sorts 4/5 vs 2/7). The sickest are the absolute bars - 20 gw-HDD, 0.50 b_share, $900 chain cum. That is the S111 condition_audit finding reproduced independently on a different eleven plays.

audits.the_argument: Claim: when aggressor flow is flat, fade the heavy resting side - an ask-heavy book means price runs UP through it, 'wall = fuel, not floor'. The entire support is one cross-sectional split in legacy_notes.evidence: ask-heavy legs go up 0.61 (n=158), bid-heavy 0.42 (n=121). That number is a real measurement and it is NOT the outcome the play was written to explain, so this is not OUTCOME_CREDITED. It is also not ASSERTED - there is a number and there is a stated mechanism. But it is a single POOLED read over 279 legs from the 12 warm-season days of S92, in direct violation of this desk's standing 'per-cell always, never pool' rule, with no per-cell breakdown, no null, no monotone-in-strength check (which the sibling direction.flow_nowcast does carry), and no replication. The play's own forward field reads 'NONE. Derived on the warm-season set; never re-tested on any later block. Zero forward evidence.' And the same evidence block records 'flow_beats_book_when_disagree 262/293 = 0.89', which scopes the play to the residual 11% of disagreement cases. I cannot classify it higher without a per-cell re-run and I cannot classify it lower without discarding a real measurement, so it is UNCLEAR and I say below exactly what would settle it.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES for the original split - 0.61/0.42 could have come back 0.50/0.50 and did not. NO for anything since: in the entire g17-g23 corpus the play has never been evaluated on a single day, so no test capable of refuting it has been run in five years of walk. The causal story ('wall = fuel') is layered on top of the correlation and was never tested against the obvious alternative (the heavy resting side is where informed capital sits and price is drawn toward it). This project's own OD history is the reason to be careful with exactly this evidence shape: CLAUDE.md records that apparent directional lifts from pooled flow reads 'were trend/base-rate artifacts (Simpson's on a trending window) and died under window/forward sweep + temporal OOS'.

A cheaper interim: serve imb_R (or an L1 depth-imbalance-at-entry surrogate) in the decision state so the play can at least be evaluated - it currently cannot be, in either direction.

audits.the_argument: Two separable arms. (i) SIZE: up-size the storage-Thursday magnitude prior. (ii) SIDE: the post-print LEG sides with the running chain, never the print sign, and the DAY NET is owned by the chain state. The SIZE arm is measurable and I measured it (below). The SIDE arm is the problem and it is the reason for the class. Its evidence field is a 10,000-character per-event narrative whose every entry has the form 'date, realized net, the chain was X, so the chain won' - the chain label is read at the same moment as the outcome, and the rule is confirmed by the outcome. Not one count in that block could have gone the other way. More telling: every counterexample produced a NEW conditioning dimension rather than a refutation. 1120 became the leg-vs-net split (S97.2); the G9 bullish-draw sells became polarity (S98.2); 0129/0205/0212 became spent-chain scoping (S101.3); the G14 blind became chain-state-is-tape-state (S102.1); 0326 became an entirely new play (magnitude.shoulder_counter_print_damping). Five successive rescues, each on n<=3. The forward field's headline '14 storage Thursdays, every one leg-sided with the running chain' is a 14/14 record for a rule the same file documents breaking at 1120, 0129 and 0326 - the 14/14 survives only because each break was first reclassified into a different arm.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: SIZE arm: YES, and I ran it - it could have come back at parity and it did not (1.65x pooled), and it DOES come back badly per-block in the two summer blocks. SIDE arm: NO. 'The chain won' is unfalsifiable once the chain can be relabelled live / spent / young / basing after the fact, and the play's own history is a record of exactly that relabelling. The leg-side arm is also not independently re-measurable from the committed corpus: g<N>_mbo_evidence.json serves three coarse phases per day (sflow / pxchg / vol), not a print-anchored decomposition, so nobody can recompute 'leg-sided with the chain' from the record even if they wanted to.

All other days: mean 510, median 440 - a real 1.65-1.67x lift pooled. But per-block, only 8 of 14 print Thursdays exceed their OWN block's non-print median, and the failure cell is sharp, seasonal and recent: g17 2/2, g18 2/2, g19 0/2, g20 2/2, g21 1/2, g22 0/2 (moves of -60 and 0 against a block median of 690 - the two smallest days in the block), g23 1/2. SIDE: a print day where the post-print leg runs against a chain label DECLARED BEFORE the print, with no post-hoc relabelling permitted. That falsifier cannot currently be written, because no artifact freezes the chain label at the open - which is precisely why the arm has survived five counterexamples.

audits.the_argument: Claim: a chain polarity flip needs an ARM (parabolic run >=~1.5-2x the prior largest swing, >=~9 sessions, plus a >=30%-off blow-off close) and a four-condition CONFIRM (C1 band-break >=1.5x, C2 old-side continuation-collapse, C3 printed-never-front-run, C4 catalyst arbiter). This is the best-supported play in the batch and the support is falsification-shaped, not narrative. The per-instance table carries counts that could have gone the other way: C1 fires 1008 / 1020 / 1208 / 1223 / 0120 / 0302 and correctly DECLINES 0107 - six fires, one correct decline, zero false positives across G4/G5/G9/G10/G11/G14. It carries a documented FALSE POSITIVE (G10 0108) and a documented FALSE NEGATIVE (G11 0120) on opposite sides of the same bar, and says so in its own text. C2's ratio reformulation was REFUTED on comparable data (0120 true 0.714 vs 0107 false 0.718, near-identical on every arm) and was KEPT-AND-SCOPED rather than quietly dropped. C2's absolute arm is explicitly declared non-discriminating above ~160 legs / 75k trades. A negative control is named (G7 1113: blow-off form fired, swing only 0.55x the prior, correctly no flip). The problem is not the support. It is that the play has been dormant for nine blocks and its requires field is wrong about the architecture it now runs in.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, repeatedly and demonstrably - this is the one play in my batch whose evidence has visibly been allowed to embarrass it. 0107 could have fired C1 and did not. 0120 could have fired C2 and did not, and the play recorded that as its own false negative rather than reclassifying it. The scale-invariant ratio reformulation was built expecting it would separate true from false, returned 0.714 vs 0.718, and the refutation was written into the play. The G11 block reversed +17,140 against a declined flip and the play absorbed that as a false negative and cut its own confidence 0.5 -> 0.4.

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO IN THE BLIND, AND THAT IS THE FINDING. C1 compares a day's dollar NET against a condition-class band. The blind's price-derived blocks are frozen at the block-anchor vintage, so the prior day's net is unavailable and C1 is permanently UNKNOWN - never true, never false. Five G22/G23 posteriors say exactly this in their own words. That directly contradicts the play's own requires field, which asserts 'NOTHING in the rule requires an intraday reveal; the rule is open-time applicable to the session AFTER the confirm'. It was open-time applicable in the architecture it was written for; it is not in the one it runs in now. Separately, the condition-class counter bands C1 is measured AGAINST are not served as a numeric table anywhere - each specialist re-derives them, which is D23's value-replacement problem in its purest form.
audits.falsifier: A counter day whose net breaks its condition-class band by >=1.5x, evaluated at the close and not front-run, that is NOT followed by a sustained polarity change - a genuine C1 false positive. Six fires and zero false positives is a real record and the falsifier is well formed. It has had no opportunity to discharge since G14 because in the blind the condition cannot be evaluated at all. TWO THINGS WOULD SETTLE IT, both cheap: serve the prior day's realized net (or the condition-class band table) in the blind state, and re-derive the bands for the modern amplitude regime, where the historical 1,800-5,010 fires sit at or above the corpus maximum day move of 2,100.

audits.the_argument: Claim: a failed counter-flush in the final 30-75 min, IN CONJUNCTION with a live structural pull state (delivery week / squeeze_watch / crowded short base), precedes squeeze ignition - 3/3 on 0130, 1223, 0129 spanning G9/G11; the flush alone is named NOISE. The retrospective around it is unusually disciplined and I want that on the record: it demotes F6 (trade-rate ramp) and F7 (VWAP posture) to NOISE because they fire on quiet-day controls, demotes F3/F4/F5 to WATCH for failing the spanning requirement, names 1128 as a 'WEAK-TELL INSTANCE, named honestly', names 1020's missing raw tape as a limit, and records G13 as a clean negative block. That is better conduct than most of the corpus. But the play underneath has the outcome-credited shape: the three instances were SELECTED as days that ignited, the pre-onset signature was found looking backwards, and when the one control that challenged it showed the flush-fail ALSO fires on quiet days (0219, 0212), the response was to ADD the conjunction limb rather than retract. The conjunction limb has never itself been varied - all three instances carry it, and no instance exists anywhere where the conjunction fired and ignition did not follow.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: PARTLY, and the part that could is real. The quiet-day controls could have shown the flush-fail was clean and they did not; that measurement was allowed to come out badly and it killed F6, F7 and the compression read. But the SURVIVING rule has no test capable of refuting it: a squeeze-regime day carrying a failed flush that did NOT ignite has never been looked for, and the controls used were quiet days which by construction lack the conjunction's second limb. The version that was falsified is not the version that was kept.

That negative test has never been run and it is the only thing separating the conjunction from a re-description of three squeeze days. audits.the_argument: Claim: in an S1-VOID shoulder (near-window normals base <=~20 gw-HDD), a print whose fundamental would trade AGAINST the running chain has its DAY NET damped toward flat, because S1-void removes the seasonal amplifier that turns a fundamental into a big directional day. The evidence field says n=1 and names the event: 0326, 'Blind sized +900 on the 0129 spent-chain-with-print form; actual +480 midday round-tripped to -60.' The exemplar IS the miss the play was written to explain, and the mechanism was chosen after the round-trip rather than tested against it. Two things are to its credit and I weighed them: it carries a real CONTROL (rejected_alternative: 0319, chain-sided in the same S1-void, delivered -1,080, which kills the broader 'damp all shoulder prints' version and forces the scoping to counter prints only), and its G16 forward note is honest that the counter arm was NOT exercised because G16 contained no counter print. So the standing is one instance, one control on a WIDER claim, and zero forward exercises of its own arm in ten sessions of merge history. It is not NOVEL_N1 because the instance is not a first sighting of something new - it is the reinterpretation of a miss.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: NO for the play's own arm. One day round-tripped and a mechanism was selected to explain the round-trip. The 0319 control could have come out otherwise and did real work, but it constrains a different, broader claim. The winter_contrast (0129/0205/0212 delivering +1,480/+540/+120) is the same three days already used to build the spent-chain rule inside daytype.storage_thursday_magnitude, so it is not an independent measurement here - it is the same evidence counted twice in two plays.

instances.what_the_state_said: STAND-DOWN, and the reasoning is the finding: 'trigger fails twice: it is scoped to an S1-VOID SHOULDER (near-window normals <= ~20 gw-HDD with no demand mass) and to a COUNTER print. This is S2 summer with the demand mass actually delivering (42.6 Bcfd), and the print is CHAIN-SIDED.' D declined on PROSE, not on the number - the ~20 gw-HDD bar was satisfied that day, as it is on every summer day

instances.what_the_day_did: The S1-void trigger fires 40 of 40 days. It cannot distinguish a shoulder from mid-summer; only the untestable word 'SHOULDER' does that, and 'shoulder' is not a served field. This is the same defect the brain already names in weather.absolute_hdd_bar_unevaluable_in_cdd_regime

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO. The trigger's only numeric bar is near-window normals base <=~20 gw-HDD, and on every HDD instrument served it fires 40 of 40 days across g20-g23 with 4-13x of headroom. The play is therefore always-on in summer, its call is 'damp toward flat', and any small day confirms it. Every one of the seven evidence entries has the identical form 'blind X, ACTUAL Y': g15 0318 blind -400 / actual +1,900; g15 0325 blind +250 / actual +660; g12 0203/0204 blind -750/-850 / actual +1,130/+1,260; g10 0107 blind -550 / actual +1,500; g9 0217 blind -800 / actual +1,890; g14 0303 blind -650 / actual +640. audits.the_argument: Claim: a 'spent covering' downgrade is a POSITIVE CLAIM and must clear a two-limb bar - (a) the exit session shows positive flow_conviction under falling price, a single final-phase give-back does NOT qualify, and (b) COT MM net WoW is flat or improving. This is a REASONING CONSTRAINT, not a directional prediction, and constraints of this kind are verified by construction plus recorded correct declines - which it has, and I verified them in the committed record rather than the prose. Its own outcome evidence is thin (n=2 weekends, both G19, both outcome-selected). What lifts it is that the constraint demonstrably bites in both directions and that its underlying variable sorts out of sample.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: The n=2 G19 evidence: no - both weekends were selected because they gapped up against the blind. The correct refusals: yes - limb (a) could have admitted the spent downgrade on 0528 and refused it instead, changing the number by zero. The assignment claim is properly verified and I checked it against an INDEPENDENT artifact (renders/ng_refine_s95/g<N>_mbo_evidence.json) rather than against the prose asserting it, and it holds exactly. The mass claim is a real distribution with a per-day table and a written falsifier. The play also records against itself twice, which is why it is not OUTCOME_CREDITED: 'D-0716: MASS was REFUTED 5x (+560 realized vs +110 forecast)' and 'on 0709 the blind fired this play BY NAME and emitted a path curve contradicting it.' Both are in the merged text.

The assignment claim would have died if the Thursday extremes and onsets clustered inside 08:00-10:30, and they do not - 10 of 14 onsets are pre-10:30 and several extremes sit in the prior evening, outside any 08:00-start window. The mass claim is a listed 14-value distribution (10% to 85%) with a written falsifier ('a group of EIA Thursdays whose pre-print share medians below about 25%'), so it is falsifiable. The MASS claim's own distribution changes state freely (10% to 85% across 14 Thursdays, IQR 34-59%), so the condition is not degenerate; the defect is the missing benchmark, not a stuck bar. audits.falsifier: Written and usable for the mass arm: 'a print day whose pre-10:30 share is trivial while the gate fired.' But the honest falsifier for the HEADLINE is different and has never been applied: state the 49.5% relative to a time-proportional or sqrt-time null. Under either null the measurement refutes the framing it was merged under, and the fix is a one-line restatement, not a retraction - the ASSIGNMENT arm is verified and worth keeping exactly as it is. The assignment arm's own falsifier is a run of Thursdays whose highs, lows and onsets sit inside 08:00-10:30; the corpus says the opposite.

audits.the_argument: Claim: burn confirms that weather-driven demand ARRIVED; it does not price it, because burn is a numerator with no balance-clearing denominator. Therefore burn may confirm, may DAMP a lean that contradicts it, but may NEVER license a directional lean of its own and must never act as a SUPPRESSOR before magnitude is derived. This is a PROHIBITION, and it was born out of the hardest event in the corpus: the retirement of its own predecessor, weather.burn_conversion_gate, on that gate's named forward test, by four specialists including its author. The mechanism is causal and checkable (a rate with no stock term cannot say whether the arriving demand clears the surplus), and it was tested with numbers that came out badly and were published anyway - D-0716 reports the balance term as 2/3 as a gate revocation and 4/7 as a standalone direction sorter and explicitly declines to claim it as one; E offers its own reformulation as 'a MEASUREMENT TO RUN, not a play to fire (n=1 clean)'; the forward field opens with the words 'HONEST AND THIN'. That is the conduct this audit exists to reward.
audits.could_evidence_have_come_out_otherwise: YES, decisively, and it did - this play exists BECAUSE the previous version's written falsifier discharged against it. The predecessor's falsifier was 'a burn-confirmed CDD add that fails to deliver, in G23+'; C-0708 found three clean up-fires in G23 delivering 0 of 3, and D-0709 found the CDD-add limb was a CONSTANT (positive 20/20 days across two groups) - a limb that never changes sign cannot gate. The successor's own numbers (2/3, 4/7) were then reported unflatteringly rather than rounded up.

audits.condition_can_change_state: NO NUMERIC BAR - it is a prohibition, not a threshold, so the state-change test does not apply in its usual form. What I can check is whether its two named inputs are stuck, and neither is: est_gas_burn_bcfd ranges 21.9-51.0 across the 60 served days of g18-g23, and storage.vs_5yr ranges 86-162 across the 40 days where it is served. Both move freely, which is the specific defect that killed the predecessor (a d_gw_cdd limb positive 20/20). grid_stack.age_days is constant at 2 on every served day, and the play declares that up front - 'D+2 stale by construction, a backward-looking instrument, labelled as such'. Declared staleness is not a hidden defect.
audits.falsifier: Written: 'a block where burn licenses a directional lean that delivers, with the balance term pointing the other way.' Note the awkwardness - the play FORBIDS the action whose success would refute it, so the falsifier can only be discharged counterfactually. That is exactly how D-0716 ran it (scoring what a burn lean would have said against what the balance term said against the actual, giving 2/3 and 4/7), so it is testable in practice. THE PLAY ITSELF HAS NEVER RUN: a full recursive grep of forecasts/ returns ZERO appearances of weather.burn_is_demand_arrival_not_direction in any posterior; it exists only in the brain, S110_MERGE_PROPOSAL_G23.json and the prior audits, because it was merged at S110 close-out after G23. G24 is its first ride. The one thing that should be settled BEFORE that ride is which limb of the balance term carries the sign.
